subject: Lexico Health — post-demo model fit recs + prompt specimen request
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@lexicohealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 8 Nov 2028 20:05:00 -0800
Subject: Lexico Health — post-demo model fit recs + prompt specimen request

Samir — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our demo + next steps so the evaluation loop is efficient: 

Summary of today's call:
- Goal: surface-summarization + triage for incoming patient intake forms, with strict PHI containment and auditability.
- Volume: ~30k submissions/month currently; peak bursts to 2k/day.
- Latency target: 300–500ms p50 for single-turn classification/summarization; batch async OK for bulk backfill.
- Constraints: cannot send raw PHI off-prem without redaction; audit trail + model versioning required.

Preliminary model recommendations (based on workload characteristics):
- rwd-llm-16k-finetune (13B family): best quality/robustness tradeoff for extractive summarization and intent classification.
- rwd-gen-7b-low-latency (7B q4): good for synchronous triage when latency is critical; lower cost but may need prompt engineering.
- rwd-phi-table-6b (specialized PHI-safe model): candidate for REDACT+TAG pipeline (run locally in Private deployment).

Benchmarks we plan to run (I'll schedule with Ben):
- Rouge/Lexical overlap on your annotated sample set
- Intent classification F1 on your taxonomy
- Latency/cost per 1k tokens across all three candidate variants

What we need from Lexico to start a scoped eval:
1) Prompt specimen set (CSV): 200–500 representative prompts across categories (summaries, triage labels, sensitive/edge cases). Add a column indicating expected redaction level (none/partial/full).
2) 25 labeled examples for each top-3 triage label for quick classifier baseline.
3) A short list of edge-case examples that must be handled (PHI formats, foreign-language fragments, unstructured attachments).
4) Confirmation on whether Private deployment is required for the initial tests (you mentioned legal will prefer it).

Attached: a prompt specimen CSV template and our redaction_guidance.pdf with examples and regex patterns we use for SSN, MRN, DOB, etc.

Next steps / timeline suggestion:
- Today: you upload specimen CSV to the Drive link (I attached).
- Mon (11/13): Redwood spins up a 2-week sandbox — we run baseline evals and return an initial benchmark_summary.xlsx.
- End of week 2: joint review, decide on Private vs Dedicated for pilot.

If procurement needs a SOW/PO early, loop in procurement@lexicohealth.com and we'll provide a short SOW and estimated cost for a 3-month pilot.

Thanks — I copied Ben and Marissa who will run the benchmarks and help with redaction rules.

—Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: lexicio_prompt_template.csv (template), redaction_guidance.pdf (attached)

Date: Fri, 9 Nov 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Lexico Health — post-demo model fit recs + prompt specimen request

Mina — appreciate the thorough recap. Quick answers and a couple of items: 

- We'll share the specimen CSV; legal flagged that any row-level PHI must either be redacted client-side or allowed under our DTA. For the initial upload we'll provide de-identified rows where possible and mark redaction_level=full for PHI-heavy samples.
- Procurement: we can likely sign a short MSA addendum for a 2-week sandbox — procurement@lexicohealth.com is looped here. They want an estimate for cost caps before legal signs off.
- Edge-cases to include: PDF images (OCR failure modes), clinician shorthand, and inbound voice->transcript artifacts.

Inline are 6 quick prompt examples to seed the CSV (we'll send a proper CSV by EOD Mon):
1) "Patient presents with chest pain and hx HTN. Summarize key concerns and triage priority."
2) "Patient denies fever. Vitals: T 98.6 F, BP 140/88. Return a 2-sentence summary for PCP."
3) "pt dob: 03/02/1956; ssn: 999-xx-1234; complaint: shortness of breath"
4) "Voice transcript: 'uh, um patient says chest, more pain when breathing... can't remember med name'"
5) "Attachment: radiology report snippet — 'possible consolidation RLL' — extract findings and next steps."
6) "Non-English: 'dolor en el pecho' — classify intent and language."

We'll try to include label columns where we can. Expect the upload to the Drive link by Mon afternoon. Procurement will follow up with a cost-cap email.

—Samir
Head of Clinical Ops
Lexico Health
samir@lexicohealth.com

Samir — perfect, thanks. Couple clarifications on the redaction guidance and the specimen file: 

Redaction guidance (practical):
- Preferred: you remove PHI client-side when possible and mark redaction_level=full. If you need Redwood to run our redaction pipeline we can do that in Private only (we won't accept raw PHI into hosted sandboxes without a DTA).
- For DOBs and SSNs in examples: replace middle digits with x's (e.g., 1956-xx-02; SSN 999-xx-1234) so we can still measure parsing quality without holding full identifiers.
- For free-text transcripts: include a "redaction_notes" column if clinical staff are unsure which spans to redact; we'll coordinate a quick review.

Specimen CSV template notes:
- Columns we need: id, raw_text, expected_output (optional), triage_label (optional), redaction_level (none/partial/full), language, source_type (form/voice/pdf).
- If you have PDFs/images, include an OCR snippet column rather than raw binary.

Attachments: I've re-attached redaction_guidance.pdf and a smaller prompt specimen template named lexicio_prompt_template.csv. Ben — when you have a minute can you confirm the baseline benchmarks you'll run and the compute estimate for the 2-week sandbox?

Thanks,
Mina

Quick note from engineering/bench team:
- Baseline plan: run three model variants (rwd-llm-16k-finetune, rwd-gen-7b-low-latency, rwd-phi-table-6b) on the 500-sample set. Metrics: summary ROUGE-L, triage label F1, hallucination flag rate, and p50/p95 latency.
- Compute estimate for 2-week sandbox: ~120 GPU hours (mixed T4/A10s) — estimated cost cap ~$8k for the pilot sandbox (can tighten with smaller sample sets).
- Deliverables: benchmark_summary.xlsx (tabbed by model), run logs, and a short regression checklist we recommend you run when you move between model versions.

Samir — if that cost/cap works for procurement we can provision Monday and start tests the same day. Otherwise we can scope to 250 samples to cut costs ~50%.

—Ben
Director, Benchmarks & Solutions
Redwood Inference
